definitions.explanation: Words expressing weakness, discouragement, or a desire to give up. Almost always used in the set phrase {弱音|よわね}を{吐|は}く (to complain, to whine).

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{一度|いちど}も{弱音|よわね}を{吐|は}かなかった。
つらい{時|とき}は{弱音|よわね}を{吐|は}いてもいいんだよと、{友達|ともだち}に{言|い}われた。
examples.english: A friend told me it's okay to let out your feelings when things are tough.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost exclusively appears in the phrase {弱音|よわね}を{吐|は}く (to whine, to show weakness). Traditionally viewed negatively, as showing weakness is often discouraged in Japanese culture. However, in modern usage, people also say {弱音|よわね}を{吐|は}いてもいい (it's okay to express your struggles).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {弱音|よわね}を{吐|は}く (to whine, to complain)
- {弱音|よわね}を{吐|は}かない (to not show weakness)
- {弱音|よわね}を{吐|は}いてもいい (it's okay to express weakness)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {愚痴|ぐち}: complaints about everyday frustrations — less about weakness, more about venting
- {泣|な}き{言|ごと}: tearful complaints — similar to {弱音|よわね} but emphasizes emotional distress
